correctness.rationale: For a vertex in part i, the actual full Laplacian column has squared norm b_i=(n-a_i)(n-a_i+1) and inner product with any class-constant zero-sum center c equal to n t_i. The unique positive-part threshold enforces zero-sum and nonnegative vertex weights; direct multiplication Lw=c. The exact distance identity puts every positively weighted vertex on the proposed sphere and all remaining vertices inside or on it. The weighted variance identity lower-bounds every competing enclosing radius by R^2+||y-c||^2; affine independence makes the barycentric certificate unique. Exact finite matrix enumerations cover 272 small profiles and 50 seeded extra profiles; numerical unrestricted center optimization verifies five examples. These experiments are not used as a proof for the infinite family.

originality.rationale: Published complete-bipartite Laplacian-simplex work determines only two-part balls and explicitly excludes full multipartite graphs. The present r>=3 theorem classifies arbitrarily many simultaneously active part classes and screened classes, plus the exact zero-weight contact boundary, by a new sorted-prefix scalar law. Braun–Meyer and Meyer–Pllaha concern basic Laplacian simplices, Ehrhart properties and coding. A complete-multipartite stable-set result has a superficially similar scalar screening method but a different vertex set, Euclidean geometry and threshold equation. Actual published-finding corpus semantic searches and checked prior own ledger claims did not disclose a dominating or equivalent assertion; historical priority remains provisional.

value.rationale: A natural complete metric classification of canonical Euclidean Laplacian simplices for all complete multipartite profiles gives an exact rational minimum sphere, every contact and clearance, a unique barycentric certificate, and an O(r log r) sorted-prefix selection rule. At the same total order 38, distinct profiles realize three, two and one positive-support classes, and an exact weak-contact boundary separates geometric contacts from optimality support. These phenomena extend beyond the previously known two-class phase and support systematic comparisons of graph-induced simplex geometry.
